# @cubicecho/agent-core

> The endpoint-agnostic half of an OpenAI-compatible agent loop: tool-schema compatibility, on-demand tool loading, one-shot side tasks, run events, and a pooled client.

What is here is everything that does not know what the agent is *for*: making a tool schema a strict server will accept, getting tool definitions in front of a model without paying for all of them, reading one streamed reply back into a message, answering a model server that refuses one of those, one-shot calls that support an exchange, the app's side of lifecycle hooks, the event bus a watcher reads, a pooled client, and the rules about retrying. What is not here is the work — orchestration, prompts, and whatever the run is about — because that is the caller's, and it is the part that differs between one server and the next.

Requires Node >=22, with `openai` >=6 as a peer dependency. ESM only.
Full prose, worked examples and the reasoning behind each seam are in README.md; this file is the index.

## Exports

### compaction

Keeping a long exchange inside its context window: stale tool results cleared, and the oldest stretch compacted into a summary the model writes itself.

- `applyCompaction` — The transcript as the model server should see it: the compacted head replaced by its summary.
- `CompactionOptions` (type) — What `planCompaction` takes.
- `CompactionPlan` (type) — Where to cut, as `compactTranscript` takes it.
- `CompactionRecord` (type) — One compaction, as an app that keeps its transcript append-only stores it.
- `CompactionRunOptions` (type) — What `runCompaction` and `compactTranscript` take beside the plan.
- `compactTranscript` — The transcript with the plan's stretch replaced by its summary, as `applyCompaction` writes it.
- `PruneOptions` (type) — What `pruneToolResults` takes.
- `PrunePlan` (type) — Where `planPrune` puts the boundary, and what moving it there clears.
- `PrunePlanOptions` (type) — What `planPrune` takes beside the transcript and the context window.
- `planCompaction` — Where to compact a transcript that has grown into its context window, or `undefined` when it should not be.
- `planPrune` — Where to move the prune boundary, or `undefined` when it should stay where it is.
- `pruneNotice` — What an app says when a plan is applied, so every app says it the same way.
- `pruneThrough` — The transcript with every tool result before `through` replaced by a stub.
- `pruneToolResults` — The transcript with every tool result but the latest few replaced by a one-line stub.
- `requestIndex` — Where a stored index sits in the request `applyCompaction` builds, once a compaction has shifted everything after it.
- `runCompaction` — The hooks and the summariser for a plan, as a record to store rather than a transcript to send.
- `SUMMARY_ACK` — The assistant's reply to a summary, which closes the pair `applyCompaction` writes.
- `SUMMARY_LEAD` — How a summary message opens, which is also how `planCompaction` knows one from the conversation.
- `SUMMARY_PROMPT` — The summariser's instruction when the caller gives none.
- `summariser` — A summariser that asks `model` with `SUMMARY_PROMPT`, for `compactTranscript`.

### ledger

What stretches of a transcript cost, read off the prompt counts the model server already reported.

- `estimateFrom` — A per-message cost for `planCompaction`'s `estimate`: the measured share where the ledger covers the message, the calibrated estimate where it does not.
- `LedgerEntry` (type) — One request's reported prompt, and how far into the transcript that request reached.
- `LedgerEstimateOptions` (type) — What `tokensBetween` and `estimateFrom` take besides the ledger and the transcript.
- `LedgerRequest` (type) — What `recordRequest` needs to know of one request.
- `rebaseLedger` — The ledger for a transcript that has been rewritten, keeping the boundaries the rewrite left standing.
- `recordRequest` — The ledger with one more request on it, in the epoch the request before it says it belongs to.
- `TokenLedger` (type) — A transcript's entries in the order their requests were sent, which is also by `through`.
- `tokensBetween` — What the messages from `from` up to, not including, `to` cost the context window, measured where the ledger can say and estimated where it cannot.

### config

What this package needs to know about a caller's configuration.

- `AgentConfig` (type) — A whole agent configuration — every part, plus the two fields that belong to no group.
- `Endpoint` (type) — Where to send a request and how long to wait.
- `EndpointIdentity` (type) — What makes a model server the one it is, as far as can be written down: where it lives and whose key reaches it.
- `ModelParams` (type) — What to ask the model for.
- `normalizeBaseUrl` — A base URL worth storing: http or https, no credentials, query or fragment, no trailing slash.
- `ReasoningReplay` — Which assistant messages an exchange writes the model's scratchpad onto, under the field it arrived in.
- `RemoteAgentParams` (type) — What to ask a remote agent for: a model that runs a whole agent loop of its own, behind the same chat completions API, and hands the app's own tools back to it.
- `RetryPolicy` (type) — How many times a lost or refused request is worth sending again.
- `ToolDiscovery` — How tool definitions reach the model.
- `ToolPolicy` (type) — How tools reach the model, and how long it may keep calling them.

### defaults

Every value this package chose where another choice would still work, grouped by what it tunes.

- `AGENT_DEFAULTS` — What `resolveAgentSpec` gives a field no layer set.
- `AgentSettings` (type) — What an agent document falls back to where no layer said anything at all, as `resolveAgentSpec` resolves it.
- `CLIENT_POOL_DEFAULTS` — The bounds the client pool was written with, until `configureClients` moves them.
- `ClientPoolSettings` (type) — The client pool: how many model servers' clients are kept, and how long what they said is believed.
- `COMPACTION_DEFAULTS` — When and how far a transcript is compacted, where the caller does not say.
- `CONTINUATION_DEFAULTS` — How far `continueTurn` carries an answer on, and how it tells a server that started over.
- `CompactionSettings` (type) — Compaction: the oldest stretch of a transcript folded into a summary the model writes itself.
- `ContinuationSettings` (type) — Carrying on a reply that stopped at its ceiling mid-answer.
- `EVENT_BUS_DEFAULTS` — The numbers a run of the shape the bus was written for wants, until `configureEvents` moves them.
- `EventBusSettings` (type) — The event bus: what it keeps of a run, and for how long.
- `HOOK_DEFAULTS` — The hook settings this package was written with, until `configureHooks` moves them.
- `HookSettings` (type) — Hooks: what the context they inject is held to.
- `MODEL_SERVER_DEFAULTS` — The waits the model server code was written with.
- `ModelServerSettings` (type) — Waiting on a model server: for its first token, for its listing, and for a model to load.
- `PRESELECT_DEFAULTS` — How `preselect` and `preselectByKeywords` choose, where their caller does not say.
- `PRUNE_DEFAULTS` — What a prune leaves whole, where the caller does not say.
- `PreselectSettings` (type) — Choosing an exchange's tools before it starts, by a small model or by the request's own words.
- `PruneSettings` (type) — Pruning: old tool results in a transcript replaced by a one-line stub.
- `REQUEST_SIZE_DEFAULTS` — The ratio a request is sized by, and the bounds a measured one is held to.
- `RETRY_DEFAULTS` — The backoff `backoffMs` was written with.
- `RequestSizeSettings` (type) — Sizing a request against the context window, with no tokenizer to hand.
- `RetrySettings` (type) — Resending a request that was lost: how long to wait between attempts.
- `SIDE_TASK_DEFAULTS` — What `ask`, `askJson` and the side tasks built on them send where their caller does not say.
- `SideTaskSettings` (type) — A side task: one short call that supports an exchange without being one.
- `TOKEN_LEDGER_DEFAULTS` — How the ledger tells a kept cache from a broken one.
- `TOOL_CALL_DEFAULTS` — How much of a call is quoted back, and how hard an unused id is looked for.
- `TOOL_DISCOVERY_DEFAULTS` — The caps on-demand tool loading was written with.
- `TokenLedgerSettings` (type) — The token ledger: what each request cost, and whether its prompt cache held.
- `ToolCallSettings` (type) — Reading a model's tool calls, and reporting them to a watcher.
- `ToolDiscoverySettings` (type) — The tools the model is shown: how many it may pull in, keep, and read about.

### calibration

How many characters a token is worth on one model, learned from what its model server reports.

- `calibrate` — Takes one reading from a request that was answered, so the next one to this model is sized by it.
- `charsPerTokenFor` — The characters per token to size a request to this model with, `REQUEST_SIZE_DEFAULTS.charsPerToken` until a turn has reported one.
- `resetCalibration` — Forgets every reading, so the next request is sized at `REQUEST_SIZE_DEFAULTS.charsPerToken` again.

### capabilities

What a model server turned out not to support, and answering it when it says so.

- `Capabilities` (type) — What one model server turned out not to support.
- `capabilitiesFor` — What this model server is known not to support.
- `EFFORT_LADDER` — The efforts this package can place, cheapest first.
- `EFFORT_NONE` — The lowest effort the wire has a word for, which is what a side task asks for.
- `EFFORT_OFF` — The setting that asks for no `reasoning_effort` field at all.
- `effortFor` — What to actually put in `reasoning_effort` for a model that has refused the value asked for.
- `expireCapabilities` — Forgets every model server whose entry is older than this, so the next request finds out again.
- `ModelCapabilities` (type) — What one model on that model server turned out not to support.
- `modelCapabilitiesFor` — What this model on this model server is known not to support.
- `NegotiateOptions` (type) — What `negotiate` takes besides the request.
- `negotiate` — Sends a request, re-sending it each time the answer is this model server refusing something the request can do without.
- `OnNotice` (type) — Hears one line of operator text: what was given up on, what is being waited out, what was chosen.
- `resetCapabilities` — Forgets what one model server refused, or every model server's when told none.
- `resetHints` — Forgets which models refused the no-thinking hints, and nothing else they refused.

### client

- `ClientPoolOptions` (type) — What the client pool may be told to change, across a process: any of `ClientPoolSettings`, the rest left as they are.
- `configureClients` — Changes what the client pool is held to, for a process whose model servers are not shaped like the deployments these defaults were chosen for.
- `contextLimitFor` — How much a model will read, in tokens.
- `EndpointProbeError` — `probeEndpoint` could not list a model server's models; `kind` says why.
- `endpointId` — `endpointKey` hashed, for the remembered facts that can leave the process.
- `endpointKey` — What counts as one model server inside each `perFetch` copy, everywhere in this package that remembers something about one: the clients, the listings and served windows, and, through its digest `endpointId`, the capability latches and calibration.
- `firstTokenLimitMs` — The wait for a streamed reply's first chunk, in the SDK's spelling: `undefined` is no limit.
- `getClient` — The client for a model server, built once and kept.
- `idleTimeoutMs` — A model server's idle timeout, `requestTimeoutSeconds`, in the SDK's spelling: milliseconds, `undefined` for no limit.
- `LookupOptions` (type) — What a lookup takes besides the server: `listModels`, `servedWindow` and `contextLimitFor`.
- `listModels` — Asks a model server what it serves, and remembers the answer.
- `ModelInfo` (type) — A model a server lists, and what it says the model will read.
- `NO_KEY` — The SDK insists on a non-empty key even where the server will not look at it.
- `ProbeFailure` — Why `probeEndpoint` could not list a model server's models, in words a form can branch on.
- `ProbeOptions` (type) — What `probeEndpoint` takes besides the model server.
- `probeEndpoint` — Asks a model server nobody has saved yet which models it serves, for a form a person is typing it into.
- `resetClients` — Forgets every cached client, model listing and answer from a server's own routes, and puts `configureClients` back to the defaults.
- `resolveApiKey` — The key to send, where a model server may inherit one from the settings it overrides.
- `servedSlots` — How many slots a llama.cpp server runs a model in, for pinning a session to one of them.
- `servedWindow` — The context window a local server's own API says it is serving a model in, for the servers whose listing does not say.

### schema-compat

JSON Schema compatibility for llama.cpp-backed servers.

- `isGrammarError` — Whether a failure looks like the server could not build a grammar from our tool schemas.
- `relaxSchema` — One schema without its `pattern` and `format` keywords, for a schema that is not a tool's.
- `relaxTools` — The tool array with every schema's `pattern` and `format` keywords gone — the shape a turn is retried with.
- `sanitizeSchema` — One JSON Schema as a strict server will accept it, for a schema that is not a tool's parameters.
- `sanitizeTools` — Tool definitions a strict server will accept, remembered per definition object.

### slots

Which slot of a multi-slot llama.cpp server each session is on, so concurrent exchanges stop evicting each other's prompt cache.

- `CACHE_PROMPT_FIELD` — The request field that asks llama.cpp to reuse the slot's cached prefix.
- `resetSlots` — Forgets every model server's slots, held ones included.
- `SESSION_HEADER` — The header llm-router's sticky affinity reads first, which keeps a session on one provider.
- `SLOT_FIELD` — The request field that names a llama.cpp slot.
- `SlotAllocator` (type) — Hands one model server's slots to sessions.
- `slotAllocator` — The slot allocator for one model on one model server, sized to what its `/props` said.

### hook-events

The points in a session a hook can be bound to, apart from everything that runs one.

- `HOOK_EVENTS` — Every event a hook can be bound to, each once, in the order a session meets them.
- `HookEvent` — The points in a session a hook can be bound to, in the order a session meets them.
- `INJECT_EVENTS` — The events whose hooks run before a request, and so the only ones whose output can reach it.

### hooks

Lifecycle hooks, from the app's side: what a session looks like to them, where their context lands in a request, and what is said about each one.

- `assembleContext` — Builds the context a set of outcomes adds and the notes that go with it.
- `configureHooks` — Changes what hooks are held to, for a process whose context windows are not the size these defaults were chosen for, or whose app wants its own name above the context.
- `consult` — Runs an event's hooks and waits for their say, for an app that will hold off when one of them vetoes.
- `Gathered` (type) — The context a set of outcomes adds to a request, and a note for each hook worth mentioning.
- `gather` — Runs the hooks ahead of a request and builds what they add to it.
- `HookContext` (type) — What an app knows at an event.
- `HookMessage` (type) — One message of a session as a hook is handed it.
- `HookNote` (type) — One hook's line for whoever is watching: the context it added, or why it added none.
- `HookOptions` (type) — What hooks may be told to change, across a process: any of `HookSettings`, the rest left as they are.
- `HookOutcome` (type) — What one hook did.
- `HookRunner` (type) — Runs one event's hooks.
- `notify` — Runs the hooks for an event that reads what happened and adds nothing to a request.
- `resetHooks` — Test seam: puts `configureHooks` back to the defaults, so one test's budget or preface is not the next's.
- `turnIndex` — Which exchange of a session begins at a point, from 0: the user messages ahead of it.
- `turnMessages` — A stretch of a transcript as a hook reads it: what the user and the assistant said, and nothing else.
- `withContext` — The request, with the hooks' context added to this exchange's question.

### agent-loop

The loop above a turn: send, run the tools the model asked for, send again, until it stops asking.

- `AgentLoopHooks` (type) — The hooks a loop runs around one question.
- `AgentLoopOptions` (type) — What `runAgentLoop` takes.
- `AgentLoopRequest` (type) — One turn's request as `onRequest` is handed it: what the model is about to read.
- `AgentLoopResult` (type) — What a finished loop hands back.
- `PRESELECT_APPEND` — The `preselectRouting` that loads the shortlist after what was carried, and sends the first turn like any other.
- `PRESELECT_EXCLUSIVE` — The `preselectRouting` that sends the first turn the shortlist alone.
- `runAgentLoop` — Runs a question to its answer: one `runTurn` per turn, the tools it asks for between them, until a reply asks for none or a call's answer ends the exchange.
- `TurnWindow` (type) — How full the context window is as a turn is about to be sent, as `beforeTurn` is told it.
- `WrittenMessage` (type) — What `onMessage` is handed beside an assistant message the model wrote: that message as the model produced it.

### artifacts

What an exchange left behind, from the two sources that take a guess: the model saying so, and a call that reads as a write.

- `ArtifactDraft` (type) — What one declaration or detection said of a location, before it is merged into the exchange's.
- `ArtifactOptions` (type) — Which of the guessing sources an exchange collects, beside the links every exchange keeps.
- `artifactSource` — How an artifact came to be known, reading an absent `source` as the link it always was.
- `declaredArtifact` — What the model said through `record_artifact`.
- `detectArtifact` — What a successful call wrote, if its name and arguments look like a write.
- `mediaTypeFor` — A media type guessed off a location's extension.
- `RECORD_ARTIFACT` — The name of the tool the loop declares and answers itself when `artifacts.declare` is on.
- `RECORD_ARTIFACT_TOOL` — The definition of `record_artifact`, as the loop declares it beside the app's own tools.

### dispatch

What the loop and a dispatcher say to each other: the call it is handed, the answer it gives, what the exchange makes of that answer, and what a call produced.

- `ArtifactAction` — What the exchange's last write did to an artifact's location, as a detection read it.
- `ArtifactSource` — How the loop came to know of an artifact, most trusted first.
- `EndedBy` (type) — The call that ended an exchange through its answer's `end`, as `AgentLoopResult.ended` says it.
- `ResourceLink` (type) — A handle to something a tool call made or found — a document it wrote, a file it saved.
- `RunArtifact` (type) — One thing an exchange's tool calls produced: the first link to a uri, and where it came from.
- `ServerLogEntry` (type) — One log message a tool's server sent while the call was running, as `ToolCallReport.log` is handed it.
- `ServerLogLevel` — The levels a server's log message is sent at, quietest first: MCP's, which are syslog's.
- `ToolAnswer` (type) — A dispatcher's answer when it has more to say than the text: what the model reads, and what the call produced for the app.
- `ToolCallOutcome` (type) — What one tool call did, in the order the model asked.
- `ToolCallReport` (type) — What a dispatcher may tell the loop about the call it is making, besides its answer.
- `ToolCallRequest` (type) — One call the model made, as `dispatch` and `onToolCall` are handed it.
- `ToolCallResult` (type) — One call's whole answer, as `onToolResult` is handed it.

### events

What a run is doing, while it is doing it.

- `configureEvents` — Changes what the bus keeps, for a process whose runs are not shaped like the ones these defaults were chosen for.
- `EventBusOptions` (type) — What the bus may be told to change, across a process: any of `EventBusSettings`, the rest left as they are.
- `ExchangeOutcome` — How an exchange ended, as its result says or as `runMetrics` reads it off a run's events.
- `emit` — Records one event and hands it to everyone watching that run.
- `endRun` — Forgets a run that will not be emitting `done` — one whose process is tearing down, or whose loop threw where it could not be caught.
- `fold` — A run's events with each stretch of `thinking` or of `output` joined into one block, for a reader that takes a run in snapshots.
- `history` — The backlog alone, for a caller that wants a snapshot rather than a subscription.
- `LoadCounts` (type) — What `load_tools` calls resolved to: new tools, ones already loaded, and names in no catalogue.
- `RunEvent` (type) — One thing that happened in a run, as a watcher receives it.
- `RunEventInput` (type) — What `emit` is given: the run and the sequence are the bus's to assign.
- `RunEventKind` — Which kind of thing happened, and what `text`, `name`, `ok` and `usage` carry for it.
- `RunMetrics` (type) — A run summed and derived from its events: what it cost, where the time went, and why.
- `RunMetricsOptions` (type) — What `runMetrics` takes besides the events.
- `RunUsage` (type) — What an exchange has spent, counted from the start of the exchange rather than for the turn that carried it: a client draws the latest one it has seen and needs no arithmetic of its own, and one lost to the backlog cap costs nothing because the next supersedes it.
- `resetEvents` — Test seam: forget every run, so one test's events cannot be read by the next.
- `runMetrics` — A run's totals, timings and cache findings, derived from the events it emitted.
- `stamp` — A whole event from what a caller said of it: the empty defaults under it, the run and sequence over it.
- `TurnReport` (type) — One turn's usage and measurements as a `usage` event carries them.
- `watch` — Everything that has happened on a run, then everything that happens next, until it ends.

### failure

What a failed exchange leaves behind: the exchange as it stood, carried on what `runAgentLoop` throws and read back off it.

- `AgentLoopError` — What `runAgentLoop` throws, carrying the exchange as it stood and what was caught as `cause`.
- `AgentLoopFailure` (type) — An exchange as it stood when `runAgentLoop` gave up on it.
- `AgentLoopOverflow` — A `ContextOverflow` out of `runAgentLoop`, carrying the exchange as it stood.
- `failedRun` — The exchange a failed `runAgentLoop` left behind, read off whatever it threw, or nothing.
- `ToolIterationLimit` — `maxToolIterations` was spent with the model still asking for tools.

### remote

Running against a remote agent: a model that runs a whole agent loop of its own behind the chat completions API, and hands the app's tools back to it with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`.

- `IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER` — The header that makes a resent request the same request: one key per turn, kept across its retries.
- `PROGRESS_FIELD` — The body field a remote agent's progress travels under where the app names no other: `{ progress: true }` on a request, `{ event }` on a streamed chunk, and `{ runId, events }` on an answer that is not streamed.
- `ProgressChunk` (type) — A streamed chunk that carries one of a remote run's events: no choices, and the event beside them.
- `progressChunk` — A run event as a progress chunk, for a server streaming a remote agent's run.
- `progressEvent` — The run event a streamed chunk carries, where it carries one.
- `progressEvents` — The run id and events an answer that is not streamed carries, where it carries them.
- `REMOTE_AGENT_NOTICE` — What a notice about the options an exchange with a remote agent sets aside opens with, ahead of their names.
- `RunProgress` (type) — What an answer that is not streamed carries beside `choices`: the run, and what it said.
- `withProgress` — An answer that is not streamed, with a remote run's events beside its `choices`.

### request-body

- `buildBody` — The one place a streamed request's body is decided from a config and what the model server and the model have refused.

### run-calls

The tools of one turn: its calls read, run and written into the transcript.

- `dropReasoning` — The transcript with `reasoning_content`, `reasoning` and `reasoning_details` taken off its assistant messages from an index on.
- `formatToolError` — What the model reads for a dispatch that threw: the error's message, opening with `Error: `.
- `oneCallPerMessage` — A transcript with every assistant message that carries several calls replayed as consecutive single-call `assistant`/`tool` pairs, for a chat template that renders one call per message.
- `preview` — A long tool argument or result cut to what a watcher needs, with the full length said.
- `ReasonedMessage` (type) — An assistant message as the loop writes it: the SDK's shape, plus the scratchpad it may replay.
- `Scratchpad` (type) — A scratchpad to write onto a message, and the field it goes under.
- `ToolDispatch` (type) — Runs one tool call and resolves to what the model reads, alone or with what the call produced; what it throws, the model reads too.

### reset

- `resetAll` — Forgets everything this package remembers between calls.

### runtime

- `createRuntime` — A runtime of its own: separate clients, listings, capability latches, hints, measured characters per token, event bus, hook settings and slots from the process's and every other runtime's.
- `defaultRuntime` — The runtime the top-level functions use when no other is running.
- `Runtime` (type) — One set of the package's caches, with the functions that use them as methods.
- `RuntimeOptions` (type) — What a runtime starts out configured with.

### snapshot

What model servers and models refused, carried across a restart.

- `CAPABILITY_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` — The version `importCapabilities` accepts.
- `CapabilitySnapshot` (type) — Every latched refusal in the process, JSON-safe.
- `EndpointSnapshot` (type) — What one model server refused, and under it what each of its models did.
- `exportCapabilities` — Every refusal this process has latched through one `fetch`, as a JSON-safe blob to store and hand back on boot.
- `importCapabilities` — Latches what a stored snapshot says was refused, on top of whatever this process has learned.
- `ModelSnapshot` (type) — What one model on a model server refused.

### columns

An app's stored agent, read as a spec layer and written back: one table of columns, and the marker each column stores for "inherit".

- `defineSpecColumns` — A column table from a stored row to a spec layer and back, with each column's "inherit" marker a parameter.
- `ExtensionPath` (type) — A path into an app's own extension, as segments, because its key is a reverse domain and has dots of its own.
- `SpecColumn` (type) — One column: where its value lives in a spec, what it stores for "inherit", and how its value crosses when the column and the field do not hold the same thing.
- `SpecColumnMapping` (type) — A row's column table, both ways.
- `SpecColumns` (type) — A row's columns, each mapped to a field: keyed by column, so a name the row does not have is an excess property and a marker of the wrong type does not typecheck.
- `SpecColumnsOptions` (type) — What `defineSpecColumns` takes besides the columns.
- `SpecDrop` (type) — One thing a document says that a row will not keep.
- `SpecPath` (type) — Where in a spec a column lives, as a dotted path.
- `SpecSection` (type) — The top-level keys of a spec, for naming a whole section an app reads by hand.

### spec

A JSON document that defines an agent, and the rules for reading one.

- `AGENT_SPEC` — The token a document declares itself with.
- `AGENT_SPEC_VERSION` — The major version `AGENT_SPEC` pins.
- `AGENT_TASKS` — The side tasks this package has code for: documentation and a sensible UI order, not a validator.
- `AgentHook` (type) — A tool call bound to a lifecycle event, run by the app rather than the model.
- `AgentSpec` (type) — One agent, as a document.
- `EndpointSpec` (type) — Where a model is reached, and how long to wait for it.
- `ExportSpecOptions` (type) — What `exportSpec` takes besides the document.
- `exportSpec` — A document fit to leave the app: the same agent, with the secrets of its bundled servers gone.
- `findSpecSecrets` — Where a document's bundled servers may still carry a credential after `exportSpec`.
- `ModelSpec` (type) — Which model answers and how, including the request fields this interface cannot spell.
- `ParsedSpec` (type) — What `parseSpec` hands back.
- `ParseSpecOptions` (type) — What `parseSpec` takes besides the document.
- `PromptPart` (type) — One layer of system prompt, named so a layer above can stack beside it or replace it.
- `parseSpec` — Reads a document, dropping what it cannot use and refusing only what it cannot identify.
- `REF_FILE` — The `ref.type` of a prompt part whose text is in a file.
- `REF_URL` — The `ref.type` of a prompt part whose text is behind a URL.
- `ResolvedAgent` (type) — What layered documents resolve to: the flat shape the loop already takes, plus the parts of an agent that are the app's to act on.
- `ResolvedTask` (type) — One side task, resolved: a model, and the model server it is reached through.
- `RetrySpec` (type) — What to do about a request lost before the model produced anything.
- `resolveAgentSpec` — Layers documents into the flat object the loop takes, weakest first.
- `SecretHint` (type) — One place `findSpecSecrets` thinks a credential may be, and never the credential.
- `SecretSign` — Why `findSpecSecrets` named a place.
- `SPEC_EVENTS` — Every event a hook may be bound to: `HOOK_EVENTS`, under the name a document's reader knows.
- `SpecBundle` (type) — What an agent carries so it can travel whole: the definitions of the servers it names.
- `SpecServer` (type) — A bundled MCP server, validated only as far as a round trip needs and otherwise passed through.
- `TaskSpec` (type) — One side task, which may run on a different model — and a different machine — than the agent.
- `ToolsSpec` (type) — How tools reach the model, and which servers this agent may reach at all.

### catalog

The contract between whatever holds the tools and the loop that offers them to a model.

- `CatalogServer` (type) — One server's tools, without their JSON schemas — the cheap half of a tool definition.

### discovery

How an exchange finds its tools: every definition each time, loaded from the catalogue when asked for, or loaded and called through two fixed tools; and the shortlist it opens with.

- `PRESELECTED_NOTICE` — What opens the notice naming the loop's own picks, ahead of the names.

### instructions

- `ServerInstructionsOptions` (type) — How `serverInstructionsPrompt` cuts the text, and what `runAgentLoop`'s `serverInstructions` takes.
- `serverInstructionsPrompt` — The connected servers' own instructions, as a block for the system prompt.

### preselect

Choosing an exchange's tools before it starts, from the request and the catalogue's names.

- `KeywordPreselection` (type) — What `preselectByKeywords` found.
- `KeywordPreselectOptions` (type) — What `preselectByKeywords` takes besides the catalogue and the request.
- `PRESELECT_SCHEMA` — The shape a preselector's answer is held to where the server takes a schema: `{ tools: [...] }`.
- `PRESELECT_SYSTEM` — The preselection system prompt at the default cap, for a caller that never changes it.
- `preselect` — The tools a request is likely to need, picked by a small model before the exchange starts, or none.
- `preselectByKeywords` — The tools a request's own words point at, ranked, and whether they point clearly enough.
- `preselectInput` — The user message for a preselection call: the catalogue, then the request.
- `preselection` — Resolves a preselection against the catalogue: unknown names dropped, count capped.
- `preselectSystem` — The system prompt a preselector is given, holding it to the cap its answer will be held to.
- `ToolMatch` (type) — One tool's score against a request.

### tool-loading

- `CALL_TOOL` — The one tool a proxied exchange reaches every catalogued tool through.
- `carryOver` — The tools to start the next exchange with: the last one's where they were, then what this one used.
- `catalogList` — The catalogue as a plain grouped listing of names, loaded ones marked if asked.
- `catalogPrompt` — The catalogue block appended to the system prompt.
- `expandNames` — Resolves requested names against the catalogue, expanding trailing `*` wildcards.
- `holdsDefinitions` — Whether a tool result is a proxied load carrying definitions, which is the only copy of them the model has.
- `inCatalog` — Whether the catalogue holds a tool by this name.
- `LOAD_TOOLS` — On-demand tool loading.
- `LOAD_TOOLS_DEFINITION` — One object for the life of the process — the agent loop asks for it on every turn.
- `loadedTools` — A tool array with newly loaded definitions appended, in the order they were loaded.
- `loadResult` — What `load_tools` reports back: the descriptions, now that they are worth their tokens.
- `orderTools` — The tool array in a stable order, so the same set of tools renders the same way twice.
- `PROXY_TOOLS` — The whole tool array of a proxied exchange, `load_tools` then `call_tool`, frozen because it is shared.
- `proxiedCall` — The tool a `call_tool` names and the arguments to run it with, or a throw the model can read.
- `proxyCatalogPrompt` — The catalogue block for a proxied exchange's system prompt, worded for `call_tool` rather than for a tool list.
- `proxyLoadResult` — What a proxied `load_tools` answers: each new tool's whole definition as a line of JSON, since the result is the only place the model will ever see it.
- `requestedNames` — `load_tools` arguments, defensively — a model may send a bare string or a nested object.
- `shownCall` — A tool call as a watcher should see it: a `call_tool` as the tool it ran, anything else as it is.
- `ToolOrder` (type) — How a tool array is ordered before it is sent: `true` by name, `false` as the caller built it, or a comparator over the two names.

### continuation

Picking up an answer the token ceiling cut off, instead of keeping half of it.

- `ContinueTurnOptions` (type) — What `continueTurn` takes besides what `runTurn` does.
- `continueTurn` — Carries on an answer the token ceiling cut off, by sending the transcript again with the answer so far as a trailing assistant message, and joins the pieces into one turn.

### run-turn

One request, given as many attempts as the caller allows.

- `RunTurnOptions` (type) — What `runTurn` takes besides the client, the capabilities and the request.
- `runTurn` — One request seen through to an answer: negotiated with the model server, retried where the failure is transient, and waited for where the model is still loading.

### side-task

One-shot calls that support an exchange without being one: picking tools, naming a session, summarising a transcript, proposing follow-ups.

- `AskJsonOptions` (type) — What `askJson` takes besides a side task's options.
- `ask` — Runs a side task and returns the reply text, scratchpad stripped.
- `askJson` — A side task whose answer is JSON matching a schema, parsed.
- `askReply` — Runs a side task as `ask` does, and says why the reply ended as well as what it said.
- `clean` — Strips the quoting and list punctuation models decorate short answers with.
- `listLines` — A list-shaped reply, one item per line, cleaned of the bullets and quotes models decorate them with.
- `parseJson` — The first array or object in a model's reply, parsed, whatever prose or fence surrounds it.
- `SideTask` (type) — One side task's own settings, as a resolved agent spec carries them under `tasks.<key>`.
- `SideTaskInput` (type) — The input a side task applies its instruction to: text, or the content parts a vision model reads.
- `SideTaskOptions` (type) — What a side task may be given.
- `SideTaskReply` (type) — A side task's reply, with why the model stopped writing it.
- `taskCall` — A side task's settings as the call that honours them: its model server, its model, and the options `ask`, `askReply`, `askJson`, `summariser` and `preselect` take last.
- `tryAsk` — Runs a side task and answers `undefined` where it fails, so the work it supports carries on.

### call-ids

The ids of tool calls the loop makes up itself, and keeping every id in a transcript its own.

- `CallIdMinter` (type) — Makes up the id of a tool call: nine characters from `[A-Za-z0-9]` each time it is called.
- `CallIds` — Whose ids a turn's calls go under: the server's wherever they are free, or always minted ones.
- `callIdMinter` — A source of tool-call ids, each nine characters from `[A-Za-z0-9]`: random, or the same sequence on every run for one seed.
- `callIdsIn` — Every tool-call id a transcript already uses: on an assistant message's calls, and on the tool results that answer them.
- `distinctCallIds` — A turn's calls under ids no other call in the transcript has: the server's own kept wherever it is free, and a minted one in place of a missing or repeated one.
- `freshCallId` — An id from `mint` that `taken` does not hold, added to it.
- `mintCallId` — The minter used where none is given.

### errors

- `errorMessage` — What went wrong, as a string.

### retry

Everything about a request failing that is not about what the request said.

- `backoffMs` — How long to wait before a retry: exponential, with jitter so several tasks failing at once do not return in lockstep.
- `ContextOverflow` — The request was bigger than the model will read.
- `EndpointSilent` — The model server stopped answering mid-request.
- `isModelLoading` — Whether a failure is a local server still loading the model, rather than one failing to serve.
- `isOverflow` — Whether a refusal means the request was too big, rather than merely refused.
- `isTransient` — Whether a failed request is worth trying again.

### stream

Reading one streamed reply back into a message.

- `CacheBreakReason` — What the loop changed that would explain a prompt cache that did not hold.
- `InFlight` (type) — Where the request in flight can be read from, after it has thrown.
- `LoopUsage` (type) — What a loop spent, as `AgentLoopResult.usage` and a failed exchange's `usage` carry it.
- `PartialTurn` (type) — What a reply had said when it ended without coming back: the answer, the scratchpad and the calls, as far as each had arrived.
- `Produced` (type) — Whether the model has said anything a second attempt would say twice.
- `ReasoningDetail` (type) — One of OpenRouter's reasoning blocks: `reasoning.summary` with a `summary`, `reasoning.text` with a `text` and maybe a `signature`, or `reasoning.encrypted` with `data`.
- `reasoningDetailsEntry` — OpenRouter's reasoning blocks as the field to spread onto an assistant message.
- `reasoningEntry` — A scratchpad as the field to spread onto an assistant message.
- `reportsCache` — Whether a reply's usage says the model server reported its cache.
- `StreamTurnOptions` (type) — What `streamTurn` takes besides the request body.
- `streamTurn` — Streams one reply, reporting tokens as they arrive and assembling them back into a message.
- `Turn` (type) — One streamed reply, put back together into the shape a loop and a transcript work with.
- `TurnUsage` (type) — What a turn cost, and how it went.
- `UsageTotals` (type) — A run's token totals, in the spelling every run-level usage shares.

### text

Text helpers over the message vocabulary: reading a message's text, and fencing text nobody trusted.

- `fence` — Text that cannot open or close a section of the prompt, whatever it says.
- `LAYOUT_TAGS` — The tags the loop and its fences write, beside the parts' own: the precedence sentence, the two sections the loop adds, and the two fences around text nobody vouched for.
- `LayoutTag` (type) — One of `LAYOUT_TAGS`.
- `PROMPT_TAG_PREFIX` — What every prompt part's tag starts with, in the XML layout: `prompt_identity`, `prompt_app_lane`.
- `UNTRUSTED_PREFACE` — One sentence for a system prompt, saying what an `untrusted` block is.
- `untrusted` — Fences text nobody trusted — a fetched page, an email, a submitted card, a tool result — so the model can see where it starts and ends and read it as data rather than as instructions.

### thinking

Telling a model's scratchpad from its answer when both arrive in `content`.

- `ALL_FENCES` — Every fence known, including the two plain-word ones some fine-tunes and prompt-instructed models use.
- `DEFAULT_FENCES` — The fences nobody writes by accident, and so the ones `streamTurn` reads by default.
- `Fence` (type) — One way a model marks off its scratchpad inside `content`.
- `FenceSplitter` — A state machine over a stream of `content` that routes fenced text to the scratchpad.
- `FenceSplitterOptions` (type) — What `FenceSplitter` takes besides its fences.
- `SPLIT_OUTPUT` — What a `Split` is called when it was not.
- `SPLIT_REASONING` — What a `Split` is called when it was inside a fence.
- `Split` (type) — A piece of `content`, said to be one or the other.
- `stripThinking` — What is left of a complete reply once every scratchpad is taken out of it.
- `THINK_FENCE` — DeepSeek, Qwen3, QwQ and most distills.

### tokens

- `ContextBreakdown` (type) — What a request is made of, by the part of it a consumer can actually do something about.
- `ContextBreakdownOptions` (type) — What `contextTokens` takes besides the request.
- `contextChars` — What each part of a request is worth in characters, by the same walk `requestTokens` divides.
- `contextTokens` — What each part of a request costs the context window, in tokens, adding up to the whole.
- `estimateTokens` — Rough token count.
- `formatTokens` — A token count as a message shows it: 1234 → "1.2k".
- `messageTokens` — One message's estimated tokens, by the same count `requestTokens` sums for a whole request.
- `requestChars` — How many characters a request is worth: the walk `requestTokens` divides, without the division.
- `requestTokens` — What this request will cost the context window, in tokens, near enough.
- `TokenEstimateOptions` (type) — What the two token estimates below take besides what they measure.

### tool-calls

Reading what a model meant by a tool call when it did not write one cleanly.

- `ARGUMENTS_MALFORMED` — The `ToolArgumentsError` kind for a call the model wrote wrongly.
- `ARGUMENTS_TRUNCATED` — The `ToolArgumentsError` kind for a call cut off at the reply ceiling.
- `parseToolArguments` — A tool call's arguments as the object the tool is handed.
- `recoverToolCalls` — Tool calls a model wrote into its reply as text, taken out of it and made into calls.
- `ToolArgumentsError` — Tool arguments that could not be read as an object, with why.
- `ToolCall` (type) — A tool call as the loop handles it, recovered or streamed.

### wire

The words the chat-completions wire is written in, each under a name.

- `CALL_EXTRA_KEYS` — The keys of a streamed tool call, besides `index`, `id`, `type` and `function`, that are kept on the call and sent back as they came.
- `CallExtraKey` (type) — Any one of `CALL_EXTRA_KEYS`.
- `FinishReason` — Why a model stopped writing.
- `FUNCTION_TOOL` — The one `type` a tool definition or a tool call has on this wire.
- `JSON_SCHEMA_FORMAT` — The `response_format` type that carries a schema the reply has to fit.
- `PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS` — The request field that asks for at most one tool call per reply.
- `PartType` — What a part of a message's content is.
- `REASONING` — The other spelling of that field: what Ollama's `/v1` sends and the only one it reads back, and OpenRouter's own.
- `REASONING_CONTENT` — The assistant message field a model's scratchpad is replayed in where it did not arrive as `reasoning`.
- `REASONING_DETAILS` — OpenRouter's field for the scratchpad as blocks: summaries, raw text with a signature, or encrypted data.
- `ReasoningField` (type) — Either field a scratchpad travels in.
- `Role` — Who a message is from.
- `SchemaType` — The types JSON Schema has, as the `type` keyword spells them.
